judged_text: Three hand-rolled copies of the fetch-credential-from-DB fallback now exist — createAllCalendarEvents (here), updateAllCalendarEvents (~505), and handleCancelBooking.ts (~424) — and they already drift: the two EventManager copies include the app relation and construct appName, while the cancellation copy fetches the bare credential with no app data. A DB-fetched credential in the cancellation path resolves through a different code path than the same credential at creation/reschedule time (no app slug available where the others construct appName), and any change to credential resolution — e.g., honoring the invalid flag, which all three copies pass through unchecked — must be replicated in three places or the flows diverge further.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce (at least) three separate “fetch credential from DB if not in memory” fallbacks with already-diverging implementations. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the fallback uses `prisma.credential.findUnique({ include: { app: { select: { slug: true }}}})` and then constructs a `credential` object containing `appName: credentialFromDB.app.slug` plus other fields. In `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents` it repeats essentially the same pattern (also including `app.slug` and constructing `appName`). In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, the fallback uses `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId }})` (no `include app`) and assigns the raw `Credential` to `calendarCredential` without constructing an `appName` field. This duplication/drift is verifiable from the diff and is a maintainability/consistency concern rather than a directly provable runtime defect from the diff alone.
